title: AI functions review: build every AI function now, baseline then learn
question: Product owner: data-driven AI must be built right now and get more accurate with time; customers must never see "arrives later because you have no data".

measure.engineWork: engineer-weeks converted at 48 points per week (Block A pace 9.6 points per developer-day); the per-operation measure prices endpoints, not engines
measure.extraPoints: Against the 29 September plan: package points for scope the plan moved past month 6 or never had, new or changed operations and screens, and engine weeks the plan does not carry

capacity.recommendation: A third AI engineer from S4 (7 Dec) gives about 16 weeks. Without one, the learned producers (9 AI-weeks) finish in shadow around May-June 2027; no tenant could pass a promotion gate before then anyway.
capacity.blockANote: Block A AI work (gateway, governance, concierge, Help me choose, translations, planner, evaluation harness) is about 13 AI-weeks against about 10 available; this is a pre-existing risk.

packageFindings: requestSuggestion is in Block A and bound to Block A screens (BO-005 queueBalancing, GST-031 prepPlan/upsell), but refuses with 422 below each kind's minimum history.
runForecast, publishForecastVersion, createForecastScenario, decideOperationalRequirement, explainMetricChange and decideAiInsight are in the Block A slice while the plan defers their producers.
Translations and the planner agent are Block A in the plan but not in the slice; ai.yaml has no planner operation and GST-054 is a deferred screen.
BO-093 Map Import & Labelling is a Block A screen without proposeVenueLabels.
evaluateAiGovernance, getAiUsage and getAiPolicy are not in the slice though Block A AI needs the decision point and spend.
team.json still says Kalpita has "no AI work in the first release"; AI operations are assigned to Hrushikant and Sanket.
No operation exists to import a venue's historical sales or attendance, and AiForecastDefinition has no cold-start setting.
cannotShipBy2April: A trained model live for a tenant: needs about a season of that tenant's data plus a 6-week shadow (or 12+ months of imported history). The code ships; promotion happens per tenant later.
Fraud classifier promotion: needs analyst-labelled confirmed cases; many tenants never reach it and stay on rules.
Learning-to-rank promotion: needs a controlled experiment with a minimum sample.
Price elasticity and AI-set prices: need observed price variation; L4 auto-optimisation stays off by governance for six months of L3 evidence.
AI dashboard and report generation (AIP-186/187): not data-dependent; an S9 stretch after the analytics assistant.

Not data questions, unchanged: external knowledge connectors (residency), partner cross-sell (integrations missing), location triggers (signals not governed), OTA/reseller recommendations (AI-D08), pooled cross-tenant models (AIP-149).

forMovingBack: Not data-dependent (design 3.12); the deferral was capacity.
The configuration assistant was the client's first AI priority (14 and 17 August, CF-57).
It collects the venue priors that make every other capability useful on day one.

The phase-2 message is marked "to be told to the client", so reversing it costs nothing with the client.

AI engineer capacity is already short without it.
assistantsDecision.recommendation: Bring both back into the six months: configuration assistant S3-S5 (seating and ticketing first), seat-map S6, analytics assistant S7. Keep AI dashboard/report generation as the only S9 stretch.

capabilities.name: Shared: the baseline-then-learn layer (built once, used by every data-driven capability)
capabilities.whatItDoesForTheCustomer: Makes every data-driven AI answer useful for a tenant with no history, and lets it improve without anyone changing a screen.
capabilities.currentPlan: Not in the plan. The design has the producer swap (SuggestionBasis, setSuggestionProvider, release pipeline) but no prior, no import and no maturity signal.

whyLeftOut.stated: n/a (new)
whyLeftOut.assessment: This is the missing piece. The contract today answers 422 InsufficientDataProblem below each kind's minimum history (8 weeks for demandForecast and anomaly, 90 days for upsell, segmentation, menuEngineering and sendTime). That 422 is exactly "this arrives later because you have no data".

approaches: rules and heuristics engine as the baseline behind the same contract
configurable venue priors entered at onboarding
import of the venue's own historical exports
TICVAI-shipped benchmark priors (synthetic or published, never other tenants' data)
Bayesian shrinkage from prior to own data

dayOne.howItWorks: One Estimator interface per question (forecast subject, suggestion kind, risk score, recommendation rank) with three implementations: prior (venue profile + benchmark pack + calendar + weather), statistical (own data, shrunk toward the prior with weight n/(n+k), re-estimated nightly), learned (per-tenant model, shadow first). The routing already exists (setSuggestionProvider, forecast definition producer, release pointer). New: a venue AI profile (capacity, opening hours, typical weekday and weekend attendance, peak months, average spend, F&B attach, staff productivity), a historical import (CSV, POS and ticketing exports, 12-36 months where the venue has them), benchmark packs per venue type (water park, theme park, family entertainment centre, museum, arena, zoo/aquarium) with the UAE calendar (Sat-Sun weekend, public holidays, Ramadan and Eid by Hijri date, school holidays, summer heat for outdoor venues), and a maturity block on every answer. Packs are TICVAI-authored from published sources and synthetic curves; no tenant data is pooled (AIP-149, design 4.2). Nightly re-estimation is not the "online learning" design 3.5 forbids: no model switches itself; each re-estimate is a recorded producer version.

maturityLadder.day1: Every capability answers from the prior; basis "heuristic", maturity "Starting", wide band.
maturityLadder.week4: Statistical producers carry most of the weight for day-of-week and short-horizon patterns; maturity "Learning"; measured accuracy appears.
maturityLadder.month3: Own level and trend dominate; the prior only fills gaps (holidays not yet seen); maturity "Established".
maturityLadder.season: Per-tenant learned producers trained weekly and run in shadow; promotion raised to the admin when the gate passes; maturity "Trained on your data" after promotion.
maturityLadder.uiShows: Every answer carries a basis chip ("Based on: your venue profile, UAE calendar, weather, 23 days of your sales") and a maturity badge (Starting, Learning, Established, Trained on your data). No bare percentages (design 5.6). A P08/P09 "AI maturity" page lists each capability, its stage, what it is based on and what the next stage needs.
maturityLadder.switchCriteria: Prior to statistical: automatic, continuous, recorded. Statistical to learned: per-capability gate (design 3.5), promotionReady alert, admin promotes (AI-D16).

capabilities.customerSentence: Every AI feature is on from your first day; it starts from your venue profile, the UAE calendar and patterns for venues like yours, and it learns your venue as you trade.

capabilities.name: Forecasting (attendance, demand, revenue, pace, scenarios)
capabilities.whatItDoesForTheCustomer: Tells managers how many guests, sales and how much revenue to expect by day, timeslot, product and channel, with a range, the drivers and a what-if simulator.
capabilities.currentPlan: B2 (4 Jan - 12 Feb 2027) "AI rules-first forecasting"; trained model after month 6. Three endpoints (runForecast, publishForecastVersion, createForecastScenario) are already in the Block A slice (SVC-AI-FORECAST-1, ADM-508, BO-919, BO-927) with no producer behind them.

whyLeftOut.stated: Six-month plan decision 2: "Data-dependent AI waits: forecasting". Earlier: 14 August minutes and the 17 August scope paper ("needs at least one full season").
whyLeftOut.assessment: True for a trained model. Not true for a useful forecast: the client's own book (AI Forecasting p.27 "New Venue / New Product Problem") asks for similar-venue, category, business-provided and rules baselines with reduced confidence. The design's first-week producer needs 8 weeks of same-weekday history or a sister venue; a new single-venue tenant has neither.

dayOne.howItWorks: Expected attendance = typical weekday/weekend attendance from the venue profile x the venue-type month curve from the benchmark pack x UAE calendar effects (public holidays, Ramadan, Eid, school holidays, summer heat for outdoor) x weather adjustment; bookings on hand act as a floor and the pace curve lifts it. Revenue = attendance x average spend (profile). P10-P90 band wide (about +/-40%) until measured. With imported history, day one starts at "Established".

maturityLadder.day1: Prior forecast with a wide band; "Starting" badge; basis "venue profile, UAE calendar, weather, bookings on hand".
maturityLadder.week4: Own day-of-week pattern and pickup curve take over (k about 4 same weekdays); accuracy measured over 28 days and shown by horizon; band narrows.
maturityLadder.month3: Seasonal smoothing on own level and trend; holiday effects still from the prior until seen; drivers from decomposition.
maturityLadder.season: Per-tenant gradient-boosted model trained weekly, shadow at least 6 weeks, then raised to the admin.
maturityLadder.uiShows: Every answer carries a basis chip ("Based on: your venue profile, UAE calendar, weather, 23 days of your sales") and a maturity badge (Starting, Learning, Established, Trained on your data). No bare percentages (design 5.6). Measured accuracy labelled "measured"; "Limited historical data" shown while the prior weight is above 50% (book p.27).
maturityLadder.switchCriteria: Automatic inside the statistical producer (prior weight falls as own data grows; recorded as a new producer version, not a model switch). Trained model: shadow for at least 6 weeks; WAPE at least 10% better than the baseline at the 7-day horizon, bias within +/-3%, P10-P90 coverage 70-90% (design 3.5). Passing raises a promotionReady governance alert; an admin promotes (AI-D16). Never automatic.

dayOne.howItWorks: Each kind gets a prior answer: replenishment = par - on hand + prior forecast use x lead time; prepPlan = prior covers x menu mix (equal shares or category benchmark); menuEngineering = margin-only ranking with popularity marked "learning"; slaTarget = benchmark default; waitTime = people ahead / configured capacity per hour; upsell = relationship map; segmentation = what is known (member, first-time or returning, party type); anomaly = configured thresholds; sendTime = channel benchmark hour; wasteRisk = shelf life and par against the prior forecast. 422 stays only when an input the venue must configure is missing, and then it names the setting, not a date.

maturityLadder.switchCriteria: The existing minimum-history numbers become the point where the own-data weight passes 50%, not a refusal. Model producers per kind are promoted by an admin.

capabilities.currentPlan: B2 "rules-first fraud"; Block A uses Orders' own rules; trained model after month 6. None of the 12 ai risk ops is in Block A.

whyLeftOut.stated: "Trained fraud models wait"; scope paper: "without labelled fraud there is nothing to detect against".
whyLeftOut.assessment: True for a classifier. Not for scoring: M21 describes a composite rule score (attempts, success ratio, cards per identity, refunds, expired-ticket reuse) that needs no history. The fraud book (Cold Start) lists deterministic rules, payment-provider signals, tenant rules, gradual learning and reduced confidence.

approaches: rules engine baseline (tenant risk strategy templates by venue type and channel)
dayOne.howItWorks: A TICVAI-authored strategy template per venue type sets velocity limits and weights; the tenant adjusts it and can backtest it once it has a few weeks of its own transactions. Fail-open with holds (AI-D06). No cross-tenant data.

maturityLadder.day1: Weighted rules plus velocity and provider signals; score 0-100 with band and reasons.
maturityLadder.week4: Entity baselines (normal behaviour per customer, device, cashier); backtestRiskStrategy on own history.
maturityLadder.month3: Graph features (shared device, token, account) and staff-leakage patterns.
maturityLadder.season: Classifier trained on analyst-labelled outcomes, in shadow; many tenants never get enough labels and stay on rules, which is acceptable.
maturityLadder.uiShows: Risk score and band, labelled "risk score", never a probability; the reasons; "rules" or "rules + model" as basis.
maturityLadder.switchCriteria: At the same review rate: recall at least equal to rules, precision at least 20% better, no segment (family, B2B, reseller) with a worse false-positive rate, over at least 6 weeks of shadow (design 3.5). Raised to admin; never automatic.
